Explanation.hint: How many points of your scale each part gives the work: the prediction as it is minus the prediction without the part
Explanation.title: Why this prediction
GradePlace.hint: Where the grade stands on your scale: a work's prediction is compared with this number
Ladder.about: Where the middles of your grades fell on the 0–10 scale. The numbers are set not by the button but by how differently the model sees the works of different grades; grades it cannot tell apart stand at one point.
Ladder.title: Your scale
ModelDetails.aucHint: How well the liked works (above “{{grade}}”) are separated from the rest: 0.5 is chance, 1 is perfect
ModelDetails.concordanceHint: The share of pairs of works with different grades the model ordered correctly (in cross-validation): 50 is chance, 100 is perfect. The parameter is chosen by it: of the values worse than the best by less than the “±”, the most cautious one is taken
ModelDetails.description: It learns order, not numbers: which of two graded works with different grades you like more. The grades themselves carry no points. The scale is built afterwards: the middle of the works with the lowest grade is 0, with the highest 10, and the other grades stand where the model put them. Texts, covers and pictures are turned into vectors; features, the sites' numbers and your actions on the sites are added to them. The parameter is chosen by cross-validation over works, by the share of pairs ordered correctly; of nearly equal ones the most cautious is taken.
ModelDetails.noImageEncoder: The picture model is not found in the models directory — covers and pictures are not taken into account.
ModelDetails.noTextEncoder: The text model is not found in the models directory — texts are not taken into account.
ModelDetails.spearmanHint: How closely the order of works by the model matches the order of your grades across all five levels: 0 is random, 1 is complete
ModelDetails.stale: Grades changed after training: the predictions lag behind. The model will retrain by itself in a few seconds, or press “Retrain”.
ModelDetails.title: Recommendation model: {{type}}
ModelDetails.untrained: The model is not trained yet: it needs at least 3 grades of at least two different kinds. Cross-validation starts from 6 graded works.
ModelsScreen.description: Everything the application works out by itself: the predicted grade, interest, the values of every site's facets. Each has a model of its own with its own settings. Here you see when and how each was last fitted, and can fit it again or search its method and settings anew.
ModelsScreen.details: More: grades, the scale, what raises and lowers a work
ModelsScreen.gradeHint: Learns from your grades and orders the works
ModelsScreen.interestHint: Learns from the marks “interesting” and “dull”; its method is its own, apart from the grades'
ModelsScreen.marks_one: on {{count, number}} mark: {{interesting, number}} interesting, {{dull, number}} not
ModelsScreen.marks_other: on {{count, number}} marks: {{interesting, number}} interesting, {{dull, number}} not
ModelsScreen.notFitted: Not fitted yet: it fits by itself once there is something to learn from
ModelsScreen.quality.AUC.hint: The share of pairs “interesting — dull” a model that had not seen them puts the interesting one first; ± standard error. The more the better
ModelsScreen.quality.CONCORDANCE.hint: The share of pairs of graded works a model that had not seen them puts in your order (on held-out folds); ± standard error. The more the better
ModelsScreen.quality.LOSS.hint: Logistic loss on held-out works: how wrong the model is about values it had not seen; ± standard error. The less the better
ModelsScreen.searchHint: Try every setting from scratch rather than refine the last; then work every item out again. Runs in the background
ModelsScreen.stale: Fitted before the latest changes; fits again after a pause
ModelsScreen.title: Models: {{type}}
ModelsScreen.walkedOn: settings refined from the last, not searched anew
ScorerComparisonDialog.compareHint: Cross-validation of every method on the current grades; nothing is saved
ScorerComparisonDialog.description: Every method goes through the same cross-validation over works on the current grades, with its own choice of parameter. The methods are computed one after another in the background, and a row is filled in as soon as its method is done; the window can be closed — the computation goes on. Nothing is saved; the main method is changed only with its button.
ScorerComparisonDialog.title: Comparing ranking methods: {{type}}
